disclaimer: City profiles give context and default inputs. Items marked verified_primary were read directly from the cited primary document by this project. Everything else is labelled in its own verification_status. Survival figures come from court-monitored inspections and news reports of specific projects and are NOT city-wide statistics.

mumbai_like.label: Mumbai-like (poor aftercare)
mumbai_like.meaning: Share of replacement trees still alive at audit. The point value 0.37 is the preset requested by the project owner. The band 0.35-0.50 spans reported outcomes for Mumbai Metro Line 3 mitigation.
mumbai_like.source: Hindustan Times, 'Aqua Line: Progress at a green price' (20 Dec 2025): only 35% of transplanted trees survived; roughly half of 20,460 compensatory saplings had survived per forest-official inspection reported to the Supreme Court (27 Oct 2025); a Bombay High Court committee found 61% of 1,643 transplanted trees dead by Nov 2019 (about 39% alive).
mumbai_like.note: Mixes transplanted mature trees (about 35-39% alive) and saplings (about 50% alive). Survival of saplings after the full seven-year period required by law may differ. Metro Line 3 is one project, not all of Mumbai.

chennai_like.label: Chennai-like (some aftercare)
chennai_like.meaning: Share of replacement trees still alive at audit. The point value 0.63 is the preset requested by the project owner and matches a reported figure for transplanted trees.
chennai_like.source: Citizen Matters / The News Minute (1 Jul 2026), 'Chennai to lose thrice as many trees as originally estimated for Metro Phase II': 63% of 1,615 transplanted trees survived, per data shared by Chennai Metro Rail Ltd.
chennai_like.note: 63% is a single reported figure for transplants. The 0.55-0.70 band around it is a project assumption (about +/-8 points), not a published range. The same article notes there is no public database on the survival of compensatory saplings.

default_survival_as_promised.note: 'As promised' assumes every replacement tree lives unless the user states a different promised survival.

survival.source: No Pune-specific survival audit was found. The range is bounded by the Mumbai-like (0.37) and Chennai-like (0.63) presets; the 0.5 point is simply the midpoint.

compensatory_planting.legal_rule: After permission to fell, the applicant must plant a number of trees equal to the estimated age of each felled tree, each at least six feet tall, within 15 days (extension up to 15 days); planted trees must survive at least seven years and any mortality must be replaced with an equal number of new trees. Applicants who cannot plant must deposit at least the valuation of the trees. New trees are to be geo-tagged and monitored.
compensatory_planting.legal_source: Maharashtra (Urban Areas) Protection and Preservation of Trees Act, 1975, s.8(5)(a), s.8(5A) and s.8(5C), as amended (consolidated text published on the Maharashtra Government/India Code portal; read directly).
compensatory_planting.legal_note: Because the statutory number depends on each tree's estimated age, there is no single fixed ratio in law; the tree officer fixes the number in the permission. Check the current amended text and any 2025-26 notification before relying on this summary. This is not legal advice.
compensatory_planting.default_promised_ratio_note: Calculator pre-fill only. Based on the Mumbai Metro Line 3 figure of about 20,460 compensatory saplings for 4,941 felled trees (about 4.1 to 1) and reused here as a placeholder because no Pune project figure was verified. Users should overwrite it with the ratio stated in their project's permission.

species_groups.note: Growth class assignments are generic expectations. Species are common examples, not a Pune tree-census result. Verify against the Urban Trees of India database and the local tree census; no shares of the city canopy are claimed.
